Lorraine Feather is a lyricist, vocalist, and composer of distinctive jazz-tinged songs in the tradition of Jon Hendricks, Dave Frishberg, and Annie Ross. She has collaborated with Dick Hyman, Stephanie Trick, and with a number of notable film directors. Her father was the well-known jazz historian and author, Leonard Feather.
Lorraine was interviewed via Zoom on March 22, 2023 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and boy am I pleased to have Lorraine Feather with me this morning. Welcome. Thanks for your time.
Thank you, Monk, for inviting me.
I’m going to introduce you as a vocalist, a lyricist, a wordsmith, and I believe a very active, creative mind.
Thank you. That’s nice of you to say.
I always put lyricist first, because I could stop singing but never writing lyrics as long as able.
I believe you did say in something I read that when you found out about being a lyricist and that you could do it —
That that was — I forget your exact words but that was the thing. That was going to be your thing.
Did I use the word thunderbolt?
Okay. That may have been it.
Possibly. Yeah. It was really something. Do you want me to tell you how that happened?
